title: Barcelona, Spain
overview: Barcelona, the cosmopolitan capital of Spain's Catalonia region, is famed for its stunning architecture by Antoni Gaudí, vibrant street life along Las Ramblas, world-class beaches, and a culinary scene that ranges from tapas bars to avant-garde restaurants. The city perfectly blends Gothic medieval history with modernist art and Mediterranean beach culture.
best_time_to_visit: May–June and September–October for warm weather, manageable crowds, and great outdoor dining. July–August is hot (30°C+) and extremely crowded. March–April is mild and affordable.
climate: Mediterranean. Hot, dry summers (28–33°C), mild winters (10–15°C). Very little rain in summer; occasional storms in autumn.

attractions.name: Sagrada Família
attractions.description: Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece and the world's most visited church under construction. The interior's stained glass is breathtaking. Book tickets 2-3 months ahead.

attractions.name: Park Güell
attractions.description: UNESCO World Heritage garden complex with Gaudí's colourful mosaic terraces and sculptural archways. Monumental Zone requires timed-entry tickets.

attractions.name: Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic)
attractions.description: Barcelona's medieval heart with narrow cobblestone streets, Roman ruins, and the Barcelona Cathedral. Free to explore; atmospheric at night.

attractions.name: La Boqueria Market
attractions.description: Famous food market on Las Ramblas with fresh produce, seafood, and tapas bars. Go early (before 10am) to avoid tourist crush. Avoid pre-prepared fruit cups.

attractions.name: Barceloneta Beach
attractions.description: City beach 10 minutes from the Gothic Quarter. Clean, lively, with beach bars (chiringuitos). Water warm June–September.

attractions.name: Casa Batlló
attractions.description: One of Gaudí's most spectacular buildings, now a world-class museum. The 'Magic Nights' show on the terrace is unmissable. Book online for discounts.

attractions.name: Montjuïc Castle & Views
attractions.description: Historic fortress atop Montjuïc hill with panoramic views of the city and harbour. Take the cable car up.

attractions.name: El Born & Picasso Museum
attractions.description: Trendy neighbourhood with the Picasso Museum (900 works), artisan shops, and some of Barcelona's best cocktail bars.

food.name: Tapas at Bar del Pla
food.description: Local favourite in El Born for classic tapas: patatas bravas, croquetas, and jamón ibérico. Busy evenings – arrive early.

food.name: La Cova Fumada (Barceloneta)
food.description: Legendary bare-bones bar where the bombas (potato croquette) were invented. Cash only, closes early afternoon.

food.name: Catalan Cuisine
food.description: Try pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato), escalivada (grilled vegetables), and crema catalana (similar to crème brûlée) at traditional restaurants.

food.name: Vermouth Hour (La Vermutería)
food.description: Spanish tradition – vermouth with olives and anchovies at 1pm. Bars in the Gràcia and Sant Pere neighbourhoods are authentic.

food.name: Disfrutar or Tickets by Albert Adrià
food.description: El Bulli alumni's molecular gastronomy restaurants. Disfrutar holds 2 Michelin stars. Book 3-6 months ahead.

transport: Excellent metro (L1–L11) and bus network. T-Casual card (10 trips, €11.35) is best value. TMB app for real-time info. Bicing bike-sharing is popular. Airport bus (Aerobús) to Plaça de Catalunya takes 35 min (~€6).

budget_guide.notes: Barcelona is moderately priced by Western European standards. Menú del día (set lunch menu) at local restaurants offers 3 courses + wine for €12–15.

tips: Beware pickpockets on Las Ramblas – keep bags in front.
Book Sagrada Família tickets months in advance to avoid long queues.
Lunch is the main meal (2-4pm); many restaurants only open for dinner from 9pm.
Learn a few Catalan words – locals appreciate 'Gràcies' over 'Gracias'.
The beach can be crowded in summer – escape to Sitges (30 min by train) for quieter shores.
